title: A finite-cover triple site for oriented products of qcqs schemes
statement:
Let $X,S,Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes and let $f:X\to S$, $g:Y\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Form $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$ as in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], using small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small skeleton [def-weil-size-convention] of the category of triples $Z=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ in which $U\to X$, $V\to S$, $W\to Y$ are separated etale morphisms of finite presentation, and the arrows are over $f,g$. Then $\mathcal C$ has finite limits, including the terminal triple $(X\to S\leftarrow Y)$. Give it the topology generated by finite jointly surjective families of types (a), (b), and the singleton families of type (c) in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Every covering family has a finite covering refinement. Restriction from the full triple site induces an equivalence $P\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, identifying the associated representable $H_Z=h_Z^\#$ on either site [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

Let $X',S',Y'$ be another such diagram with quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes and arrows $f',g'$, and let $a:X'\to X$, $b:S'\to S$, $d:Y'\to Y$ satisfy $fa=bf'$ and $gd=bg'$. Let $u:P'\to P$ be the induced geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism, lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. For every triple $Z$ above, componentwise scheme base change [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a triple
$$Z'=(U\times_X X'\to V\times_S S'\leftarrow W\times_Y Y')$$
in the corresponding finite-cover site for $P'$, and there is a canonical isomorphism $u^{-1}H_Z\simeq H_{Z'}$.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.1 (three covering types), 1.6 (inverse image of associated triple representables), 1.9 (functoriality), and proof of Lemma 2.5, printed pp. 171–175, 178–179 (PDF pp. 177–181, 184–185): the finite-cover triple presentation for coherent sites. Scheme specialization also in Orgogozo, Modifications et cycles proches sur une base générale, §8.1, printed p. 17.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-qcqs-etale-finitary-site] to $X,S,Y$. Write $E_X,E_S,E_Y$ for the resulting sites. Their inclusions in the full small etale sites preserve finite limits and induce restriction equivalences. Base change along $f,g$ restricts to finite-limit and cover-preserving functors $E_S\to E_X,E_Y$. These functors present the usual etale inverse images: the direct images on the full sites are evaluation on scheme base changes by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]. Consequently, under restriction equivalences the direct images are exactly precomposition with the restricted functors. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] their left adjoints exist and are left exact, and uniqueness of a left adjoint identifies them with $f^{-1},g^{-1}$. For later use the same argument applies to every $e:T'\to T$ between the qcqs schemes in the statement. For $A\in E(T)$ and a sheaf $F$ on $E(T')$, adjunction, [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] give $\operatorname{Hom}(e^{-1}h_A^\#,F)=F(A\times_TT')=\operatorname{Hom}(h_{A\times_TT'}^\#,F)$. Thus $e^{-1}h_A^\#\cong h_{A\times_TT'}^\#$, naturally in $A$, including its structural arrows.

source.place: XI 1.1, input sites; ordinary site adjunction supplied by Stacks Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism).

proof.text: The category of triples formed from $E_X,E_S,E_Y$ is precisely the category in the statement, before passage to a skeleton. The identity objects of the three input sites give its terminal object $(X\to S\leftarrow Y)$. Given $Z_i\to Z_0$ for $i=1,2$, take $(U_1\times_{U_0}U_2\to V_1\times_{V_0}V_2\leftarrow W_1\times_{W_0}W_2)$. Its components remain in the three input categories by [lem-trf-qcqs-etale-finitary-site]. The structural arrows exist because base change along $f,g$ preserves these limits; the three componentwise universal properties give the universal property among triples. Final objects and pullbacks imply all finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks]. Transport these limits to the chosen small skeleton using [def-weil-size-convention]; the displayed terminal triple means its chosen representative, up to its specified isomorphism.

source.place: XI 1.1; proof of Lemma 2.5, first paragraph. Finite-limit criterion: Stacks Tag 002O (lemma-finite-limits-exist).

proof.text: Let $\mathrm{Cov}(Z)$ consist of families obtained from isomorphisms and finitely many successive compositions of the three specified kinds of generating families. Types (a),(b) are stable under pullback because the ordinary input covering families are so by [lem-trf-qcqs-etale-finitary-site]. If a type-(c) arrow replaces $V$ by $V_1\to V$ with the given lift from $U$, pulling it back along $Z_0\to Z$ replaces the middle object by $V_1\times_VV_0$ and the right object by $W_0\times_{Y\times_SV_0}(Y\times_S(V_1\times_VV_0))$. The lift from $U_0$ is obtained by pairing its maps to $V_1$ and $V_0$. This is again type (c), and all components remain in the input categories by step 2. Pullbacks commute with composites by their universal properties. Thus $\mathrm{Cov}$ satisfies isomorphism, composition and pullback axioms and is a pretopology. Every family in it is finite: a composite has index set a finite union of finite sets. By [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition], every covering sieve for the generated topology contains a family from $\mathrm{Cov}$. In particular, the sieve generated by any covering family contains such a finite family, and each of its arrows factors through a member of the original family. This gives exactly the required finite covering refinement.

source.place: Proof of XI Lemma 2.5, printed p. 179: Cov(Z) and the pretopology axioms; Stacks Tag 00ZC (lemma-site-gives-topology).

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] hold for $E_X,E_S,E_Y$ by step 1: they are small sites with finite limits and pretopologies, and $f^{-1},g^{-1}$ extend the displayed continuous finite-limit-preserving functors. Its triple topology is exactly the topology of step 3, since the input pretopologies use finite jointly surjective covers. Hence $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, with its projections and $2$-morphism, is an oriented product of the usual three etale topoi. The same theorem gives site independence and identifies it with $P$ formed from the full small etale sites. This has used the already established oriented-product construction, not an unstated general coherence theorem.

source.place: XI 1.1, Theorem 1.4 and Definition 1.7; proof of Lemma 2.5, first paragraph.

proof.text: Let $r:P\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be the canonical equivalence of universal oriented products obtained in step 4. The inverse-image formula of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], applied to $r$, gives $r^{-1}H_Z^{\mathcal C}\cong p_1^{-1}h_U^\#\times_{(gp_2)^{-1}h_V^\#}p_2^{-1}h_W^\#$. The same formula applied to $\mathrm{id}_P$ identifies this fibre product, including its maps, with $H_Z^{\mathrm{full}}$. For any full-site sheaf $F$, adjunction, [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] now give $(r_*F)(Z)=\operatorname{Hom}(H_Z^{\mathcal C},r_*F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H_Z^{\mathrm{full}},F)=F(Z)$. These bijections are natural in $Z$ and $F$, so $r_*$ is naturally isomorphic to restriction to the restricted triple site. Applying the direct-image quasi-inverse of $r^{-1}$ to the generator isomorphism gives $H_Z^{\mathrm{full}}|_{\mathcal C}\cong H_Z^{\mathcal C}$. This proves the requested restriction equivalence and representable identification without asserting that the triple topology is subcanonical.

source.place: XI 1.3, formula (1.a) of 1.6 and Definition 1.7; site adjunction: Stacks Tag 00X6.

proof.text: Apply the base-change clause of [lem-trf-qcqs-etale-finitary-site] to $a,b,d$. It puts $U'=U\times_XX'$, $V'=V\times_SS'$, $W'=W\times_YY'$ in $E(X'),E(S'),E(Y')$. The map $U'\to V'$ is induced by $U'\to U\to V$ and $U'\to X'\xrightarrow{f'}S'$; their composites into $S$ agree by $fa=bf'$. The corresponding pair with $gd=bg'$ gives $W'\to V'$. These are precisely the two structural arrows of the claimed triple. In particular no quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis on $a,b,d$ has been used: separated etale finite presentation is stable under arbitrary scheme base change.

source.place: XI 1.9, applied to a commuting diagram of schemes; ordinary scheme-base-change clause of the cited input.

proof.text: Use the inverse-image formula in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] for the universal map $u:P'\to P$ induced by the commuting diagram. With $A=a p'_1$ and $B=d p'_2$ it reads $u^{-1}H_Z\cong A^{-1}h_U^\#\times_{(gB)^{-1}h_V^\#}B^{-1}h_W^\#$. By step 1 the component inverse images are $a^{-1}h_U^\#=h_{U'}^\#$, $b^{-1}h_V^\#=h_{V'}^\#$ and $d^{-1}h_W^\#=h_{W'}^\#$, with their structural arrows. The equalities $fa=bf'$ and $gd=bg'$ and the canonical composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] identify the displayed fibre product with $p_1'^{-1}h_{U'}^\#\times_{(g'p'_2)^{-1}h_{V'}^\#}p_2'^{-1}h_{W'}^\#$. The left map is the structural $U'\to f'^{-1}V'$ followed by the inverse-image mate of the primed oriented $2$-morphism, since the $2$-morphism defining $u$ is obtained by applying $b$ to that primed $2$-morphism and pasting the two commuting squares. This fixes the direction and the map into the middle factor. Apply the same universal formula to $\mathrm{id}_{P'}$ and the triple $Z'$: the resulting fibre product is $H_{Z'}$. Composition gives $u^{-1}H_Z\cong H_{Z'}$. All comparisons came from natural adjunction and pullback maps, so this is the canonical isomorphism on both equivalent presentations of step 5.

source.place: XI formula (1.a) of 1.6 and functoriality 1.9; ordinary inverse-image composition: Stacks Tag 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q22-3954d3be2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and found no fault, so no fixes and no drop_nodes. Sources checked: ILO XI 1.1-1.11 and 2.4-2.5 (PDF pp. 177-185), and Stacks 021D, 04HR, 01KU, 01KV and 01TS (all tags correct). New node lem-trf-qcqs-etale-finitary-site: true, statement-only, self-contained and searched. E(T) (separated étale finite-presentation maps to a qcqs T) contains T. It is closed under fibre products, because A->C is étale, separated by 01KV, and of finite presentation by qc/qs cancellation. Every étale U->T is covered by affines, which lie in E(T), so finite refinements exist and the 04HR comparison gives Sh(T_Et)=Sh(E(T)). Its clauses are stable under any base change between qcqs schemes. Tested on: the empty T, non-separated qcqs T (the identity is in E(T)), and non-affine T, where an affine-only site would lack the terminal object. rg over the DAG and the main-20261015 blueprint found no duplicate: the affine-étale-site, single-cover refinement, generic dense-subsite and finitary-coherent nodes all state less. The node is about one scheme, so it does not restate the item. Item: statement unchanged and not weakened. Step 1 shows the restricted direct image is precomposition, gets the left adjoint from left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor, and gets e^{-1}h_A^#=h^#_{A x T'} from adjunction, Yoneda and sheafification. Step 2 takes limits componentwise. In step 3 I recomputed the pullback of a type (c) map, and it is again type (c), so Cov is XI 2.5's finite-composite pretopology. Step 4 checks every hypothesis of oriented-product-universal for both the E-sites and the full sites, then uses site independence. Step 5 computes r^{-1}H^C_Z=H^full_Z, so r_* is restriction. Step 6 checks fa=bf' and gd=bg' give the structural arrows. Step 7 uses the XI 1.6/1.9 formula with A=a p1', B=d p2' and 2-arrow b(tau'), plus the composition-unit isomorphisms; the direction of the left map is correct. The fit with the parent was checked (Y=S, g=id). Route: the off-unit units sk-def-exchange, sk-thm-properbasechange and sk-thm-iff are all in the transitive route of sk-i-curve-zero. The two declared tool_uses are therefore unnecessary but harmless, and I accept them. This is not a target node, and the coefficients are sheaves of sets as in ILO.
